newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil won't put economic stability at risk.
newsitem.headline: Brazil won't put economic stability at risk.

text.p: The Brazilian government will not allow a potential 28.9 percent wage claim from the federal work force to put economic stability at risk, a presidential spokesman said.

Spokesman Sergio Amaral told reporters the government would take steps if a high court ruling granting the wage hike to 11 civil servants was extended to the full federal workforce, adding the government was also studying an appeal.

"The government will not put economic stability at risk and will have to take other measures should the decision, which only applies to 11 civil servants, be extended to other public sector workers," Amaral said.
"This is a legal challange and (the government's lawyers) are studying whether or not it is possible (to appeal)," he added.
Amaral did not specify when asked what those measures could be, but it was clear he was referring to cost-cutting measures.
Earlier, the Supreme Federal Tribunal ruled in favour of 11 public sector workers who claimed they were entitled to a 28.9 percent pay rise awarded to the armed forces in 1993.
The ruling could set a precedent for up to one million other civil servants, who would each have to bring their own case against the government, workers' lawyers said.
The government said it had no idea of the potential cost of the ruling, but newspapers have put it at $7.0 billion a year in extra payroll spending and $20 billion in backdated pay.
